previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted for surgical management of class III morbid obesity (BMI ~40) with comorbid obstructive sleep apnea on CPAP and gastroesophageal reflux. She underwent a laparoscopic Roux-en-Y gastric bypass with intraoperative endoscopy and recovered without complications, initially requiring Dilaudid PCA for pain control before transitioning to oral Roxicet. An upper GI study confirmed no anastomotic leak or obstruction, allowing staged diet advancement to Stage III, which she tolerated well. Port sites remained dry, the JP drain was removed without difficulty, and she ambulated independently; she was discharged home with instructions to crush all pills, avoid NSAIDs, continue CPAP, remain on Stage III diet until surgical follow-up in 2 weeks, and take prescribed medications including Protonix, Actigall, and Colace with return precautions for concerning symptoms.
problems: Body Mass Index 40 and over, adult

Brief Hospital Course:
The patient was admitted to the General Surgery service on 
___. CBC and electrolytes, as well as Vitals and Ins/Outs 
were all closely monitored and the approprite repletions and 
treatments were insitituted throughout her stay at the hospital. 


___: A CT scan was done which demonstrated oral contrast in 
the gastric pouch and gastric remnant suggesting fistulous 
communication between both. Up to 3.5 cm dilatation of the 
proximal efferent limb was also note, though it was stated to be 
of unclear etiology. No obstruction was noted. An EGD was done 
which demonstrated that the gastric pouch was unremarkable. The 
GJ anastomosis appeared widely patent and within 2 cm of the 
anastomosis on the jejunal side, two ulcers were noted. An 8mm 
superficial clean-based ulcer was noted proximally and a 1.5cm 
deep cratered ulcer with a flat pigmented spot at the center was 
noted distally. No active bleeding was noted. The afferent and 
efferent limbs were entered and appeared unremarkable. An H. 
Pylori serum test was also sent which was found to be negative. 
The patient's pain was controlled on IV morphine. The patient 
was started on Protonix 40 IV qDay. 

___: The patient was placed on a Bariatric 2 diet and she 
was switched from IV medications to PO Roxicet for pain control. 
She tolerated modifications to diet as well as to pain control.  


___: The patient's diet was advanced to a Bariatric stage 
III diet. The patient reports that she was having a slight 
amount of loose stools late in the evening.

___: The patient was switched to a lactose free diet to 
address the patient's diarrhea. The patient was also given 
Protonix PO instead of IV. After the patient was found to be 
tolerating oral food and medications, and the pain was well 
controlled, the patient was discharged home with appripriate 
follow-up.

radiology_notes.text:
INDICATION:  ___ woman with history of gastric bypass surgery,
presents with epigastric pain, now about two months after surgery.  Please
evaluate for anastomotic ulcer.

TECHNIQUE:  Contiguous MDCT images through the abdomen and pelvis were
obtained after administration of oral and intravenous contrast.

COMPARISON:  Upper GI barium study from ___.

FINDINGS:

CT OF THE ABDOMEN:  There is mild bibasilar atelectasis.  The liver is normal.
The gallbladder is normal.  There is no intra- or extra-hepatic biliary
dilatation.  The pancreas, spleen, and bilateral adrenal glands are normal. 
There is a right extrarenal pelvis.  The left ureter is slightly prominent
without evidence of obstructing stones.

No retroperitoneal or mesenteric lymphadenopathy.  There is no free air and no
free fluid.  Oral contrast is seen in both the gastric pouch and the gastric
remnant suggesting fistulous communication between both.  Oral contrast is
both visualized in the efferent as well as the afferent limb of the Roux-en-Y.
There is up to 3.5 cm dilatation of the proximal efferent limb of unclear
etiology.
The distal anastomosis site with Roux-en-Y appears normal without evidence of
obstruction or leak.

CT OF THE PELVIS:  The urinary bladder, vagina and uterus appear normal. 
There are no pelvic hernias.  There is no pelvic lymphadenopathy.  There is no
free fluid in the pelvis.

BONES:  No suspicious lytic or sclerotic bony lesions.

IMPRESSION:
1. Oral contrast is seen in both the gastric pouch and the gastric remnant
suggesting fistulous communication between both. 
2.  Upper GI Gastrografin study is recommmended for confirmation. 
3.  Up to 3.5 cm dilatation of the proximal efferent limb, of unclear
etiology. No obstruction.
